blurb: A unit reaches each declaration of a used commons by one spelling: the bare name its `uses` brings in, the alias (`uses lib.billing as B`, then `B.Amount`), or the full name (`lib.billing.Amount`). Reading the same declaration by a second spelling would make two names for one type, so the compiler refuses the second and names the one to keep. Use that spelling everywhere, or change the `uses` clauses so that only one spelling reaches it.
summary: A declaration of a used commons is read by a second spelling in one unit (a selected name beside its alias-qualified or full-name form); a type's identity is its name, so the second would be another type.
